title: Assembling the inverse-image half of an ordinary semilinear system
statement: Let J and J′ be essentially small sites with a common coefficient universe; let B_n and F_n be strict towers of commutative ring sheaves, with adjacent transitions τ and σ [def-coef-semilinear-system-models]. Let L be a finite-limit-preserving functor on set sheaves, and I_n specified algebraic inverse images of B_n into F_n, compatible with τ and σ on underlying ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-algebraic-inverse-image]. Assume I_n.modules preserves finite limits and finite colimits at every n. There exists an OrdinaryInverseSystem: an exact functor on the actual sequence-site module categories with level I_n.modules; its evaluation isomorphisms are identity on component section carriers. Restriction of coefficient actions commutes with I_n by a comparison whose underlying map is the identity under moduleUnderlying. For every n≤m, the horizontal transition of the image system, under evaluation, is I_m of the original transition followed by this normalized coefficient-restriction comparison. This asserts only inverse image, not any right adjoint, unit or direct-image construction.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03D2 and 03DA; Zheng Construction 4.1, termwise inverse-image construction. Complete Lean construction by H2, 2026-10-26, using the existing normalized restriction comparison and strict-system/sequence-site equivalence.

proof.text: The adjacent compatible ring squares define a natural transformation between the underlying set-sheaf towers, using NatTrans.ofOpSequence. Its naturality gives the scalar square for every n≤m. Apply the proved inverse-image scalar-restriction comparison to obtain restriction comparisons normalized by moduleUnderlying; take the inverse orientation required here and cancel its underlying isomorphism to prove the normalization.

On StrictRingSystem, define the image levels as I_n.modules and the transition as I_m of the old transition followed by the normalized restriction comparison. The underlying transition is the old underlying map under uInv conjugated by moduleUnderlying. The underlying old transitions form a functor from the opposite natural-number poset. Its identity and composition laws, functoriality of uInv, and cancellation of moduleUnderlying prove the strict laws. Naturality of the restriction comparison and the old system map square prove the morphism compatibility. This constructs the functor explicitly.

Use the proved ordinary source strict-system construction, whose levels and transitions are exactly evaluation and transition. Reassemble the transported strict system using strictSystemSequenceEquivalence. Compare its evaluation with the transported level by pushforwardCongr and strictSystemSequenceUnitLevel; these comparisons are identity on section carriers. The section formula of the old transition shows that reassembly has precisely the transported transition, proving the required transition equation. The strict evaluations jointly reflect isomorphisms and preserve finite limits and colimits, so Mathlib JointlyReflectIsomorphisms.jointlyReflectsLimit and jointlyReflectsColimit detect preservation by the transported functor from preservation at every level. Reassembly is an equivalence and hence preserves both kinds of finite (co)limits.

theorem ordinaryInverseSystem_exists [PreservesFiniteLimits uInv]
    [∀ n, PreservesFiniteLimits (I n).modules]
    [∀ n, PreservesFiniteColimits (I n).modules]
    (hI : ∀ n,
      uInv.map ((sheafCompose J (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{max c v r})).map (τ n)) ≫
          (I n).ringUnderlying.hom =
        (I (n + 1)).ringUnderlying.hom ≫
          (sheafCompose J' (CategoryTheory.forget CommRingCat.{max c v r})).map (σ n)) :
    Nonempty (OrdinaryInverseSystem.{c, v, r} J B τ J' uInv F σ I)
